title: Calibrating the correlation does not fix the copula: the family moves a standardized contrast by up to 0.03 on the log odds and log hazard scales
question: Once a Gaussian copula's correlation is calibrated to the reported correlations, can the remaining error from copula family (asymmetry and tail dependence) move a target-standardized contrast?
design: Population-level numerical study: three covariates with normal or skewed margins, true Clayton, Gumbel or t copula at Pearson correlation 0.3 or 0.6, against calibrated and uncalibrated Gaussian and alternative-family reconstructions; identity, logit, log and complementary log-log links; integration order by randomized quasi-Monte Carlo.
answer: Yes, modestly on the log odds and log hazard scales and strongly on the log rate scale. With margins and correlation matched, the calibrated Gaussian erred by up to 0.034 on the log odds ratio and 0.032 on the log cumulative hazard ratio (above 0.02 in 5 of 16 primary cells), with opposite signs for lower- and upper-tail dependence, and by up to 0.63 on the log rate ratio. The error plateaued by 256 integration points. A wrong flexible family was worse than the Gaussian in 61% of comparisons, so the defensible report is an envelope over families.
findings: Identity link: every error exactly zero, as the second-order argument requires.
Uncalibrated versus calibrated Gaussian: at most 0.001 apart on the logit and complementary log-log scales.
Envelope over five families contained a t-copula truth outside them in 22 of 24 cells, median width 0.044.
Matched-correlation control narrowly failed: 0.0057 against a 0.005 tolerance, within the check's Monte Carlo error.
not_answered: Population-level; three exchangeable covariates with common margins; no mixed or discrete margins, vines or reconstruction uncertainty. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Target-standardized marginal contrast on the link scale
methods_compared: alternative copula families calibrated to the same correlation
n_sim: Population-level calculation: 10^6 draws per joint law, 2 margins x 2 correlations x 6 families
